title: Sell the Company, Keep the Archive?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A company sale and an archive transfer can be designed as separate but coordinated transactions; what may or should be separated depends on ownership, contracts, duties, taxes, privacy, culture, and jurisdiction.
The record separates the material dress, House of Worth attribution, Charles Frederick Worth design credit, accession, and the museum’s present custody.

01 · PERIMETER — What exactly is in the deal?. Inventory entity interests and each asset class with current owner, custodian, governing record, restriction, liability, and desired treatment. Do not infer asset ownership from brand presentation.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · TRANSFER — What mechanism moves each asset?. Distinguish equity sale, asset sale, trademark assignment, copyright transfer, license, loan, deposit, donation, data transfer, and services or transition arrangement.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · ARCHIVE — What must remain connected?. Map originals and copies, provenance, restrictions, operational dependencies, privacy, legal hold, contributor access, research terms, correction, and future interpretation.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · AFTER — Who can use and explain the history?. Define access, digitization, exhibition, licensing, publication, brand reference, authentication, enforcement cooperation, funding, custody, and dispute mechanisms.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

Attach title, assignment, license, consent, privacy, and custody evidence.
Run operational, research, worker, collaborator, customer, and public-interest consequences.
Take the actual deal structure to transaction, IP, privacy, tax, employment, and archive specialists.
